catalysts.headline: Q4 FY2026 results (fiscal year ended Sept. 30, 2026): GAAP EPS $8.12 (revenue $657.05M, +27.4% YoY, beat $652.35M consensus); non-GAAP EPS $11.10 (vs. $7.74 a year earlier), beat $10.89 consensus by 4.6%. GAAP results absorbed a $65 million accrual for a proposed antitrust class-action settlement tied to the Scores business and a $27 million restructuring charge for workforce reductions, partly offset by a $48 million gain on sale of a minority equity investment. Company withheld FY2027 guidance while negotiating customized mortgage-pricing arrangements for calendar 2027

Q4 FY2026 results included a $65M accrual for a proposed Scores antitrust-litigation settlement, a $48M non-operating gain on sale of an equity stake, and a $27M restructuring charge; management declined to give FY2027 guidance citing mortgage-market uncertainty

FICO reported Q4 FY2026 results (quarter ended 2026-09-30): revenue $657M (+27.3% YoY vs $516M PY); GAAP net income $175.0M / diluted EPS $8.12 (vs $155.0M / $6.42 PY); operating cash flow $294.2M (vs $223.7M PY). Results included three disclosed one-time items: a $65M accrual for a proposed settlement of antitrust class actions tied to the Scores business, a $48M non-operating gain from the sale of an equity investment, and a $27M restructuring charge tied to a workforce reduction.

catalysts.headline: Wave of analyst actions the same week: Wells Fargo downgraded FICO to Equal Weight (PT cut to $735 from $800), shares fell a further ~7.5% intraday; JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral (PT cut to $900 from $1,530); UBS cut PT to $942 from $1,100; BMO Capital kept Outperform but cut PT to $897 from $1,150; Mizuho kept Outperform but cut PT to $1,063 from $1,344; BofA, by contrast, raised its PT slightly to $720 from $700.

FICO shares fell more than 13% after FHFA Director Bill Pulte said the agency was focused on 'more action' on mortgage credit-score competition, reigniting VantageScore-competition concerns (same storyline as the Sept 29 crash).
catalysts.source: Yahoo Finance, 'FICO stock falls 14% after Pulte pledges more action on credit score competition'

catalysts.headline: FICO shares reported up roughly 16% over the week of Oct 12-19, 2026 to about $771, with 'no clear new catalyst' identified by the source; a partial rebound from the Sept 29, 2026 FHFA/VantageScore-driven crash (close $617.87)
catalysts.impact: Partial recovery, but price target cuts across Wall Street in the same window per the source

catalysts.headline: FHFA (under Trump administration direction) and HUD green-light a single, unified Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac loan-level pricing grid covering both Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0, removing the prior 20-point downward score adjustment VantageScore carried; ends FICO's structural mortgage-scoring pricing advantage. Classic FICO remains required for manually underwritten loans; FICO 10T is not yet approved for GSE delivery.
catalysts.impact: FICO shares fell approximately 27% on the news

catalysts.headline: FHFA director Bill Pulte announces Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will adopt a single loan-level pricing-adjustment grid covering both FICO and VantageScore for conventional mortgages, ending the structural pricing advantage that had forced lenders to rely almost exclusively on FICO scores; TransUnion also extended discounted VantageScore pricing through late 2028 and the largest U.S. mortgage lender named VantageScore its new preferred score
catalysts.impact: FICO shares fell approximately 25-27% (worst S&P 500 performer that day; described as steepest one-day decline in 6+ years)

catalysts.headline: FHFA Director Bill Pulte announced Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will move to a single LLPA pricing grid covering loans scored with either Classic FICO or VantageScore 4.0, removing the prior 20-point pricing adjustment distinction; no effective date or replacement grid was published
catalysts.impact: stock closed -26.52% at $617.87 (4:00 PM EDT); other sources cite -20% to -27%

catalysts.headline: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac expanded VantageScore 4.0 availability to all approved lenders, removing the prior requirement for written approval

FICO shares fell sharply (reported ~27% by one source, ~17% by another) after the FHFA director announced plans for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to merge their two mortgage credit-score pricing grids into one, with VantageScore added alongside FICO Classic - seen as a threat to FICO's mortgage-scoring position; no start date or new pricing schedule had been announced per the coverage found

notes: The $65M accrual disclosed Nov. 4, 2026 is for a PROPOSED antitrust CLASS-ACTION SETTLEMENT specifically tied to the Scores business - this is distinct from (though related in subject matter to) the long-running Sky Federal Credit Union-led monopolization litigation before Judge Edmond Chang (N.D. Ill.), which as of the last confirmed ruling found (November 2024) allowed Sherman Act monopolization and state-law claims to proceed against FICO while dismissing claims against the credit bureaus and other claims with prejudice. No 2025-2026 docket update, trial date, or settlement terms for the Chang litigation itself were found in this pass; the $65M figure may or may not relate to that specific case versus one of the other ~10 related antitrust suits Chang is overseeing. Separately, the September 2026 FHFA/VantageScore mortgage-pricing development is a material, dated regulatory risk that predates but likely still weighs on the stock heading into Nov. 11. Recommend a follow-up pass specifically on court dockets (Law360/Bloomberg Law) to identify which case the $65M settlement accrual actually covers.
